problem: PatientDetailPage mixes dashboard data fan-in with a longitudinal clinical-history editor and its retry-safe write workflow.
desired_outcome: Place the clinical-history UI and its controlled draft, pending, idempotency, and read-back confirmation behavior in a domain feature slice while keeping patient loading and cross-dashboard projection in the page.
user_journey: Open a patient record and review the longitudinal clinical-history summary.
Expand the history section and edit the existing draft or create one for the current encounter.
Save while an encounter is writable and wait for the API write and a fresh read to confirm the exact entry.
If confirmation fails, retain the draft and show an error so the user can retry.
If the patient route changes while saving, ignore the stale completion and reset the feature state for the new patient.

current_evidence.claim: The page currently owns the clinical-history draft, save pending flag, idempotency attempt, save handler, route-generation guard, and exact read-back match.
Existing page tests cover create confirmation, closed-encounter read-only behavior, stale read-back preservation, route change during save, and stale patient responses.
The application is a Vue 3 Vite SPA and owns accordion expansion and page-level action feedback outside the history feature.

unknowns.question: Does keyboard focus and announcement behavior remain correct in a real browser and with assistive technology after extraction?
unknowns.falsification: Run the deployed browser journey with keyboard-only navigation and an assistive-technology pass.

unknowns.question: Does the extraction preserve the current patient detail appearance across narrow viewports and dark theme?
unknowns.falsification: Compare browser screenshots for light and dark themes at desktop and narrow viewport widths.

constraints: The API remains the source of truth for clinical entries.
Keep the route-generation guard so a stale patient response cannot update the active view.
Retain the current page-level accordion order and stable trigger and panel IDs.
A successful message requires a fresh read-back matching the patient, encounter, record, title, content, deletion state, and increasing version for updates.
No added request, persistence mechanism, permission rule, or optimistic success behavior.

render_environment.server: API owns authorization, persistence, and clinical-entry truth
render_environment.client: Patient route composes the feature; the feature owns its controlled draft and save workflow
render_environment.hydration: No SSR hydration boundary is used for this route

browser_targets: Current evergreen browsers supported by the app
ux_invariants: The history summary and preview reflect the same controlled draft.
The save action is disabled when the focused encounter cannot be edited.
An unconfirmed write keeps the draft available for retry.
Changing patient routes prevents a previous save from reporting success for the new patient.
accessibility_invariants: The accordion button exposes expanded state and a stable controlled region.
The region remains labelled by the trigger.
The textarea remains keyboard-operable and the save control exposes pending state through the design-system button.
data_invariants: The page remains the owner of loaded patient and encounter projections.
The feature only adopts saved content after exact read-back confirmation.
Mutation retry reuses its idempotency key only for the unchanged payload.

selected_pattern: Domain feature card with a controlled view contract and feature-owned form/save workflow
selection_rationale: The history card and write protocol form one recognizable patient-domain journey.
The page remains the owner of patient route loading, accordion navigation order, global feedback, and cross-card server projections.
The feature owns draft, pending, and retry idempotency state; it returns only an exact reread-confirmed entity.
No server/query cache, request identity, authorization, persistence, or visual redesign is introduced.

illegal_states: write while no writable focal encounter exists
stale patient completion mutating the current route
state_contract.owner: Feature owns form/save lifecycle; page owns route guard and accordion expansion

data_fetching_contract.query_identity: Existing patient route ID and selected encounter ID
data_fetching_contract.deduplication: No query cache or new fetch path
data_fetching_contract.cancellation: Existing page-generation guard ignores stale patient work; network request is not aborted
data_fetching_contract.stale_policy: Only an exact fresh listEntries result can confirm and replace the draft
data_fetching_contract.error_policy: Propagate a recoverable error to page-level alert and keep the draft

mutation_semantics.idempotency: Reuse one generated idempotency key while the serialized mutation payload is unchanged; generate a new key for edited payload
mutation_semantics.pending: Feature saving ref drives the design-system button pending state
mutation_semantics.duplicate_guard: Saving control prevents repeated user submission; service idempotency protects retries
mutation_semantics.optimistic: No optimistic server projection or success message
mutation_semantics.rollback: No local server-state write occurs before confirmation; failed save retains draft
mutation_semantics.invalidation: Existing listEntries reread confirms persisted state and the page merges the confirmed entry

loading_behavior: Patient page retains its current loading skeleton; history pending state applies only during save.
empty_behavior: No existing history shows the current empty summary and an empty editable draft when the encounter is writable.
error_behavior: The page displays the existing action error; a failed write or stale read-back never replaces the draft or announces success.
recovery_behavior: User edits or retries; unchanged payload reuses the idempotency key; changed payload gets a new key; route change resets feature state and rejects stale completion.
responsive_behavior: Retain the current card grid, full-width open-card behavior, textarea resize, and existing narrow-screen layout.
keyboard_focus_behavior: Keep current arrow/home/end navigation order by forwarding the history trigger keydown event to the page-owned usePatientCards handler.
assistive_behavior: Preserve button expanded/controls state, labelled region, textarea semantics, and DsButton busy semantics.
motion_behavior: No new motion or transition is introduced.

performance_budget.workload: One clinical-history field within the patient detail dashboard
performance_budget.baseline: Existing patient route and save/read-back request sequence
performance_budget.target: No increase in route requests or loaded dependencies; smaller page module through domain extraction
performance_budget.hard_max: Preserve existing request count and route loading behavior
performance_budget.measurement: Compare module composition and focused tests; browser bundle measurement remains pending

bundle_impact: Adds no package or service dependency; component and composable remain in the existing patient route chunk.
rendering_impact: No route-level rendering mode change; controlled draft updates rerender the feature view.
network_impact: Preserves the existing create/update followed by one listEntries confirmation request.
security_implications: Clinical text remains rendered as escaped Vue interpolation; no HTML rendering is added.
The client-side canWrite flag only controls the UI; the existing API remains responsible for authorization.
The composable preserves patient, encounter, and record identity matching on read-back.

testing_requirements.claim: Create/update payloads, idempotency retry, route staleness, exact read-back confirmation, and retained draft behavior remain correct.
Controlled edit, expanded/region semantics, read-only behavior, pending, and action events remain correct.
Confirmed entries still update page projections and global success/error feedback; route change ignores stale save.

runtime_evidence_required: Patient route change during pending save
performance_evidence_required: Route chunk size comparison only if bundle splitting is proposed

migration.strategy: Extract the existing history card and workflow in place without changing service DTOs or page route ownership.
migration.compatibility_window: No API compatibility window required; existing DOM IDs and service contracts remain stable.
migration.rollback: Restore inline markup and workflow from the parent component if focused tests reveal a behavior regression.

rollout: Ship as an internal Vue component/composable refactor behind the existing route with no feature flag.

unresolved_risks.revalidation: Before claiming full browser or accessibility acceptance for M-22.
